Then, calculate the discriminant (Δ = b² - 4ac). If Δ > 0, there are two real and distinct solutions, which can be found using the quadratic formula x = [-b ± √(Δ)] / (2a). If Δ = 0, there is one real solution, x = -b / (2a). If Δ < 0, there are no real solutions.

To find the stationary points of a function y = f(x), first, find the first derivative of the function, f'(x). Set the first derivative equal to zero and solve for x to find the critical points. Then, find the second derivative of the function, f''(x), and evaluate it at each critical point. If f''(x) > 0, the function has a local minimum at that point. If f''(x) < 0, the function has a local maximum at that point. If f''(x) = 0, the test is inconclusive, and other methods must be used to determine the nature of the stationary point.
